brief: A sturdy step for my toddler to stand on so they can reach the bathroom sink.

requirements.requirement: A step a toddler can stand on to reach the bathroom sink
requirements.evidence: Built a two-level stool: three hex bases on the floor level (0,0,0), (1,0,0), (0,1,0), plus two bases stacked on the first two (0,0,1) and (1,0,1). The top is about 160 mm above the floor (measure y=160). Footprint is about 334 x 335 mm. I have not verified this height against a real sink or toddler, and the stool has no handrail or non-slip surface.

Checks are clear (meshClash clear, no error issues). The floor bases are locked with two M6 joint bolts (one per wall of the floor triangle) so they can't slide apart. The stacked tiers rest on stacking collars/double snaps. The BOM calls for 8 M6 bolts and nuts. Structural strength depends on the printed material (PETG per the BOM notes) and on tightening the bolts by hand to about 2 N.m. I cannot verify material strength or load rating from the configurator.

finish.summary: The build is a 160 mm tall, roughly triangular two-tier hex stool with a 2-cell-wide top. The configurator reports no errors and a clear mesh check. Height suitability for the sink and the toddler, the material, and the strength under load are not something the configurator can confirm. Note: the floor triangle has bolts on two of its three walls, and the top two tiers are not bolted to each other. Before use, assemble the bolts by hand and check the stool with the child.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
